Hi Olga / Ben,

Thanks for the kickoff call earlier. We captured the initial requirements in the attached spreadsheet (acme_requirements.xlsx) but wanted to follow up with a concise list of constraints from our side before we get to a formal plan: 

- We require BYOK import into our VPC-hosted HSM; vendor-signed import token acceptable.
- Import ceremony needs customer operator present — we will not hand over unwrapped key material.
- Network: the HSM will be on a private VLAN with only management via the private peering. No public IPs.
- Audit evidence: we need a pre-provisioning checklist and an end‑to‑ceremony attestation (signed PDF).
- Rotation: preference for 90–180 day DEK rotation, but open to zero-downtime rewrap approach.

Can Redwood outline how you handle the wrapping key lifecycle, operator separation (Redwood vs customer), and whether you provide an import helper or expect us to use vendor tooling? Also list the HSM models you support for onprem BYOK imports.

John from our infra team will coordinate availability for the ceremony.

Thanks,
Acme SecOps

Hi team — thanks for the clear constraints, that helps. Summary of Redwood's proposed approach (high level) and a couple of options so we can pick the least disruptive one for your ops model: 

1) Supported HSMs & import formats
   - We support vendor import formats for Thales Luna and nCipher nShield (PKCS#11 wrapped import / vendor import tokens). If you have a different HSM vendor, please share the vendor KB and we'll validate.

2) BYOK import and wrapping key lifecycle (recommended)
   - Customer generates DEK locally and wraps it with a short‑lived ephemeral wrapping key (EWK) that is itself imported into the HSM via vendor import tooling.
   - Redwood can provide a transient import helper script (runs in your VPC) which performs the wrapping under your operator's control; the helper never sends unwrapped DEKs out of your environment.
   - We recommend: EWK rotation every 30 days; DEK rotation cadence we can set per bucket/tenant (default 90 days). EWK rotation prevents long‑term exposure of the import envelope.

3) Ceremony / operator separation
   - Ceremony is a two‑party process: one customer operator (on your side) and one Redwood operator (remote via recorded session). Customer holds the plaintext DEK; Redwood will never possess the plaintext.
   - All steps are recorded and an attestation PDF is produced and uploaded to the shared drive. We provide a playbook and checklist (attached: operator_ceremony_playbook.pdf).

4) Network & zero‑downtime rewrap
   - We support private peering and PrivateLink style connectivity. HSM management plane must be restricted to the peered subnet and a dedicated management bastion (no public IP). See network_spec_v1.pdf for port/VLAN recommendations.
   - For DEK rotation we use a rewrap workflow: new key is imported and data is rewrapped with live traffic using the KMS rewrap API; we can coordinate a rolling rewrap by shard to meet your availability SLOs.

5) Audit & evidence
   - Redwood will produce: pre‑ceremony checklist, signed attestation PDF, operator session recording (encrypted in our audit bucket), and the import manifest (hashes, timestamps). We will place artifacts in the shared drive link below.

Next steps we propose:
- Confirm HSM vendor (Thales or nCipher preferred) and whether you want Redwood's import helper or to run vendor tooling.
- Pick 2‑hour window for the ceremony (we recommend 10:00–12:00 PT).
- Share the customer operator's short authorization list and the emergency contact for oncall.

I copied Mina (Security & Controls) and Ben (Private Deploy) so they can validate the procedure against our compliance guardrails.

Attachments: operator_ceremony_playbook.pdf, network_spec_v1.pdf

Best,

Hi all — quick vendor note from HSMCo:

- We can produce supplier import tokens for Thales and nCipher formats; tokens are single‑use and tied to the import manifest.
- Attestation: we support signed import receipts (vendor signed) that include key fingerprints and timestamps; these can be used alongside Redwood's attestation for an out‑of‑band audit trail.
- Import helper: we provide a validated import client that runs in the customer's environment; Redwood's helper is fine so long as it's executed under your operator's account and the binary is verified.

KB: https://kb.hsmco.com/import-formats#redwood (contains sample manifests and expected vendor receipts).

If you want, we can pre‑stage a token for the ceremony once we have the manifest (hashes) — forward the manifest to tokens@hsmco.com and we'll provision.

Regards,
Chris Lang

- HSMCo: pre‑stage import token once customer provides manifest; contact tokens@hsmco.com (owner: Chris).
- Redwood: provide import helper package and playbook; schedule 2‑hour ceremony and produce attestation artifacts (owner: Olga).

Design notes / constraints to accept ahead of ceremony:
- Redwood will not hold plaintext DEKs at any time.
- Import helper must run in customer VPC and be executed by customer operator account.
- Temporal window: EWK rotation recommended 30 days; DEK default rotation 90 days unless you request 180.
